memory_candidates.content: When mechanically migrating many shell test suites onto a shared library (sourcing lib/common.sh), do not detect 'already sources the library' by substring-matching the library's path anywhere in the file. A suite that merely copies the library into a fixture (`cp .../lib/common.sh ...`) or checks its existence in a dependency-presence test contains the substring without actually sourcing it. Require a regex match on an actual top-level `source`/`.` statement naming the library. The failure mode this produces -- removed local helper definitions plus undefined replacement calls under `set -uo pipefail` without `set -e` -- fails SILENTLY (exit 0, 0 recorded assertions) rather than crashing, and is caught only by a before/after output diff, never by a syntax check.

A phase-commit wrapper's containment self-check that builds a glob pattern by string-concatenating '/*' onto a file_scope entry can silently produce a double-slash pattern (and therefore match nothing) when the entry already ends in a trailing '/'. Any file_scope that mixes bare directory entries ending in '/' with exact-file entries is at risk; verify such a wrapper's dropped-path warnings are empty before trusting a phase commit's file count, and recover an incomplete commit with an explicit follow-up git-commit-scoped.sh call naming the exact dropped paths rather than widening the pathspec.
